source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Sterling NVA4 publishes 11 MW of IT capacity, which is 0.7% of Virginia's disclosed 1,603 MW and ranks 22nd among the 25 Virginia facilities that publish any capacity at all.

Virginia has 330 mapped data center facilities, and only 25 of them disclose a capacity figure. The state's published capacity total therefore rests on a small, self-selecting subset, and a real, operating campus can be almost invisible in the aggregate. NVA4 is one of those: a named CyrusOne asset with a facility code, a campus designation, and a published load, sitting near the bottom of the disclosed set.

For AI, the number that matters is power rather than floor space. The facility pairs 11 MW with 128,715 square feet of technical space, which at 40 kW per rack implies roughly 275 racks. That is a modest load by the standards of the training campuses that drive near-term grid contention, so this site adds to Virginia's demand without shaping the bottleneck. Whether it can draw more power depends on grid supply, interconnection queue position, and operator capital plans, none of which are published here.

The data covers disclosed size and operator type and little else. There are no certifications, no street address, and no announced expansion, which is also the single input the suitability score of 57 records as missing. Coordinates are zeroed, so the record does not place the building precisely. Read this as a snapshot of what one operator chose to publish, not as a measure of the site's trajectory or its claim on the grid.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
